title: Shopper Support Desk Guidance — Agent Approval Limits for Cartwise Shopper Batches Pay Adjustments
content:
Pay adjustments on Cartwise Shopper Batches are limited across all of a shopper's batches. The agent may approve an adjustment only while the number of pay adjustments booked across all batches of the same shopper contractor account in the rolling 30 calendar days ending on the handling date (counted by each adjustment's booking date) is below the batch type's number of adjustments the agent may approve per 30 days, **and** the adjustment is not above the batch type's largest single adjustment the agent may approve. Otherwise the dispute is escalated (its status becomes escalated) and no adjustment is booked by the agent.

## The two limits

- **The 30-day count** is kept per shopper contractor account, across every batch of that account, not per batch. It is read from the system's record of booked pay adjustments before the new one is approved.
- **The single-adjustment cap** is the figure of the batch type of the batch being adjusted, and "not above" means an adjustment exactly equal to the cap is within it.

Both figures are the batch type's schedule values for the agent's approval cap and the per-30-day count.

## Decision table

| Adjustments already booked in the rolling 30 days | Adjustment amount against the batch type's cap | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Below the per-30-day figure | Not above the cap (equal counts as not above) | The agent may approve and book it |
| Below the per-30-day figure | Above the cap | Escalated; no adjustment booked by the agent |
| At or above the per-30-day figure | Not above the cap | Escalated; no adjustment booked by the agent |
| At or above the per-30-day figure | Above the cap | Escalated; no adjustment booked by the agent |

## Boundary illustrations (hypothetical figures)

Take a hypothetical batch type whose cap is 15.00 and whose per-30-day figure is 3.

- Two adjustments booked in the window and a new adjustment of 15.00: the count (2) is below 3 and 15.00 is not above 15.00, so the agent may approve it.
- Two adjustments booked and a new adjustment of 15.01: above the cap, so the dispute is escalated.
- Three adjustments booked and a new adjustment of 4.00: the count is not below 3, so the dispute is escalated.
